meta.title: Rust from scratch
meta.eyebrow: Six weeks, five hours a week
meta.subtitle: From the first cargo new to a published command line tool
meta.description: A path from zero to Rust, ending with a CLI of your own.

phases.title: The language basics
phases.summary: Syntax, types and the ownership model.

nodes.title: Setup and first project
nodes.summary: Install the toolchain and learn what cargo does for you.
nodes.challenge: Create a project, run cargo run and leave cargo clippy with no warnings.
nodes.success: You know what each cargo command does.

nodes.title: Ownership and borrowing
nodes.summary: What sets Rust apart: who owns each value and for how long.
nodes.challenge: Rewrite a small program fixing every compiler error without using clone.
nodes.success: You can explain why the compiler refused each piece.

nodes.title: Moves and copies
nodes.summary: What happens when a value changes owner.

nodes.title: References and lifetimes
nodes.summary: Lending without giving the value away.

nodes.title: Lifetime elision
nodes.summary: When the compiler works it out on its own.

nodes.title: A look at unsafe
nodes.summary: Just to know it exists and when it shows up.

nodes.title: Error handling
nodes.challenge: Read a config file and return useful error messages for every possible failure.
nodes.success: No unwrap is left in your code.

nodes.title: Traits and generics
nodes.challenge: Define a trait for output formats and implement two of them.
nodes.success: You pick between generics and dyn for a reason.

nodes.title: The CLI
nodes.summary: Put it all together in a tool you would use.
nodes.challenge: A CLI that reads a file, transforms it and writes the result, with tests.

nodes.title: Publish
nodes.summary: Document, version and publish on crates.io.
nodes.success: Someone installs your tool with cargo install.
